{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment is neutral or negative (sentiment <= 0.00) to correct for overconfidence in upward moves.",
    "Reduce forecast volatility in early periods (e.g., first 5 days) when price is trending downward — avoid overreacting to recent spikes.",
    "When true outcome is significantly higher than forecast (overshoot), reduce subsequent forecast by 5–10% to account for mean reversion or market correction.",
    "If forecast peaks sharply after a low, apply a lag correction: delay peak by 1–2 days and reduce amplitude by 10–15% to avoid overestimating momentum.",
    "In periods with sentiment > 0.25, increase forecast volatility but cap upward moves at 5% above recent high to prevent over-optimism.",
    "When true outcome shows strong downward trend (e.g., >3 consecutive days below 60), reduce forecast by 10–15% to reflect mean reversion.",
    "For long-term forecasts (30-day), apply a smoothing filter: average last 3–5 true outcomes to reduce noise and avoid overfitting to recent spikes."
  ]
}
